I'm English so I've never seen anyone shoot someone over the eventual distribution of funds from a deceased persons estate but it can get ugly as fuck! It literally tears families apart.

I used to work for a gas and electric utilities company handling the accounts of dead people. It was depressing as fuck walking in to work each morning to a stack of death certificates on my desk but nothing was more depressing than seeing that the deceased person had no will and their estate was being handled by a probate lawyer.

One case I handled had been dragging on for 13 fucking years!!

It always got ugly and was never fun to deal with. Everyone and their dog had to fight for a piece of whatever was left behind and the laws regarding who gets what are ridiculous. Debts always come first and the family left behind that may have been expecting to inherit something specific can often be left disappointed.

You need to specify who gets what down to the last penny or it will turn into a familial fist fight or a situation like this video!!

Just remember though, even if you create a will saying "this person gets x, this person gets y and this person gets z", if you have debts when you die then anything valuable can and will be sold to pay those debts regardless! Your house, car, jewellery etc might not end up with the person you want it to go to as it could be sold to cover what you owed when you died.

If you know you have outstanding debts then your will should also specify what exactly you would like to be sold to clear those debts before you consider who you would like to leave your belongings to.

Don't promise a certain item to anyone if it's worth a lot and you have debts because the chances are they won't get it and it will result in a legal battle!

As an accountant I find this distressing. Levying a tax like this would be a nightmare. Why? Because rich people don't just have a giant room full of excess cash. They have a relatively small amount of cash and cash equivalents, with the majority of their wealth in more long term non liquid investments.

Take Trumps own finances. I haven't seen the most recent filling he did, but before that he put out a balance sheet like summary of his finances. 8+ billion net worth, only like 250 million in cash/equivalents. A 15% tax on his net with would force him to sell off assets. People worth 10 million can't just pull 1.5m cash out of their asses.

I find it hard to believe he wouldn't be aware of that.

A lot of these guys have a lot of stock. Picketty shows the asset distribution and stock is a big part of the portfolio, even if it is owner stock that is less liquid. It is not difficult to get a stock transfer tax in place, so the stock would not be sold on the open market but could change ownership. Then there would be real assets (stock) rather than promise of future payment behind debt. That would change the nature of that debt precipitously.

Yah stock is relatively liquid in most cases, but the upheaval that would result from all the Warren buffets of the US selling their a stock to cover their bill would be nuts. The market would be flooded, man prices would drop precipitously. You'd have people selling 50m worth of stock to cover 35m in tax. Theyd take huge losses in terms of value, and have to pay cap gains on top of it all lol.

They wouldn't have to sell, as I mentioned, only transfer ownership. It would not have to go to the market as a liquidity producer. No tax would have to be paid in any case because there is little or no capital gains tax, and usually what people sell is offset by other losses, hence no "gains" and no "tax". This would be a transfer of wealth rather than a "tax".
